diagnosis: Primary stacks show the Source API thread inside HttpBundleTransport.read -> verify_bundle (sequential raw-file loop, up to max_records=500 reads, each up to a 20s transport timeout) -> _pull_ordered -> run_frontier_item -> run_scheduled, while the controller waits on _request_json (30s urlopen timeout) from run_schedule_tick. Per-pull work was bounded by record count only, not elapsed time, so a steady pull could outlive the controller request. Which item and the latency distribution remain UNKNOWN.
change: CollectorBundleAdapter.read_budget_seconds (default 15s) is a whole-pull raw read budget. verify_bundle(deadline=) stops fetching raw files once exceeded (always at least one read) and records verified_through; _pull_ordered returns only verified rows with the existing partial cursor '<key>|items=<n>' and complete=False, leaving the rest pending. Controller timeout not inflated; no new queue/service.
preserved: Every returned row's raw hash/size is still verified; cursor/ack only via existing delivery persistence; hash/size mismatches in later slices still raise; no_new_data requires fully verified boundary.

tests.result: 368 passed, 1 skipped (deterministic fake clock, no sleeping)
tests.old_fails_new_passes: test_slow_reads_make_bounded_scheduler_progress_and_persist_partial_cursor fails with the budget disabled (verified), passes with it. Connector-level budget tests set the budget explicitly so they do not independently demonstrate old-fails.

limitations: A single raw read can still take up to the transport's 20s timeout, and index/manifest/items reads are not budgeted; worst-case pull is about budget + one read + metadata reads, which can approach the 30s controller timeout for a very slow host.
Several connectors in one scheduler request each get their own 15s budget; overlapping-request/in-flight-execution handling in the controller was not changed.
No hosted/VM/live verification performed; real latency distribution unknown.
